_comment: Committed and versioned deliberately. A caller that invents its own
tasks per run can pick ones that flatter the candidate, which is the
measurement equivalent of grading your own exam. These are the same
PROTECTED tasks are the holdout. Do not tune against them, do not read
them while iterating, and do not add a protected task that duplicates a
development one -- a holdout that measures what you already optimised
Every task counts something that should go DOWN, so direction is
lower_is_better throughout. There is no task counting tests or lines:
those reward volume, and a candidate can always add more of either.
All four are research_tool. There is deliberately no investment_return
task, because there are no attributable outcomes yet. Adding one before
those exist would let a tooling improvement be spent as an economic
claim, which is exactly what the domain split prevents.
